one_month_reasoning: In-window events: FCX Q3 2026 results (expected ~Oct 22, 2026, historical pattern; some calendars say Oct 15) with first 2027 volume/cost color and Grasberg Block Cave ramp status; Escondida supervisors' union strike vote (Sept 28-30) outcome and any strike; unresolved US refined-copper tariff decision (Comex carries a tariff premium over LME). Q2 was a clean beat (adj EPS $0.74 vs $0.59) and H2 volumes are guided >20% above H1, so an operational beat is plausible, but copper sits at record highs ($6.83/lb Comex Sept 22) with LME stocks rebuilding ~20% since mid-August, and the stock jumped 4.5% on Sept 30, so near-term reversal risk offsets. Net: roughly symmetric, a small positive drift (median ~$70.9) at monthly vol ~13.5% (48%/3.5), slightly widened for the earnings print.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (2027E EPS ~$4.30 x 17x = $73) and EV/EBITDA (2028 run-rate EBITDA ~$17B at mid-cycle ~$5.75/lb copper x 7x, less ~$5.3B net debt incl. downstream and ~$15B NCI value, /1.443B shares = ~$69), weighted 60/40 toward P/E.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus 2027 EPS $4.14 (24/7 Wall St., Sept 2026) nudged up because copper spot (~$6.6-6.8/lb) is above the $6.00 guidance deck; cross-check: management EBITDA ~$16.5B at $6 copper interpolated from ~$13B at $5 / ~$20B at $7, less ~$2.4B DD&A and ~$0.3B interest, ~40% tax, ~25% minority share => ~$6.2B / 1.443B shares = ~$4.30.
FCX trades at ~18x forward (24/7 Wall St.); applied a slight discount because 2027 earnings are on near-record copper that sell-side (Goldman ~$11,500/t avg) does not expect to persist.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2028 run-rate EBITDA $17B x 7x = $119B; less net debt $2.1B + downstream debt $3.2B and ~$15B NCI market value => $99B / 1.443B = ~$69

inputs_detail.derivation: Management sensitivity ~$13B at $5 and ~$20B at $7 copper (~$390M per 10c); Grasberg reaching full capacity by end-2027 (PTFI avg 1.6B lbs 2027-29) lifts volume; applied at mid-cycle ~$5.75/lb given Goldman's view that >$13,000/t is not sustained.
Mid-cycle multiple for a diversified copper major; current ~7.5x on 2027 by same arithmetic; no premium for jurisdiction risk (Indonesia IUPK post-2041 still under negotiation).
FCX owns 48.76% of PTFI (economic share higher until 2022 cost recovery closed) plus minorities at Cerro Verde/Morenci; approximated as ~25% of equity-level earnings capitalised at the same multiple.

bear.story: Copper mean-reverts toward $4.75-5.00/lb as tariff premium unwinds, LME stocks rebuild and the AI data-center capex story cools; Grasberg Block Cave ramp slips again (as in Q1 2026 guide cut). 2027 EPS ~$2.60 at 17x.

base.story: Copper holds $5.75-6.50/lb on Chilean supply problems (Codelco H1 output -10%, Escondida labor, acid shortage) and electrification demand; Grasberg reaches ~80% by mid-2027 on schedule; EPS run-rate ~$4.3-4.6 at 16-17x.

bull.story: Structural deficit persists, copper $7+/lb, Grasberg at full capacity by late 2027, leach program adds volume, buybacks accelerate; EPS ~$5.7 (street high) at ~20x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$48 (-32%) the market would be pricing either a collapse in copper back below ~$5/lb or a second major Grasberg setback / adverse Indonesian permit terms; that is beyond ordinary 48%-vol noise over a few months and would mean the ramp-plus-price thesis failed.

reasoning: Alternative-lane research (Substack newsletters, independent analysis sites, prediction-market check, Indonesian-language press) points to a copper market at record highs ($14,779-14,833/t LME, $6.83/lb Comex in Sept 2026) driven by Chilean supply problems, an acid bottleneck and a US tariff premium, with visible fragility: LME stocks up ~20% since mid-August and Comex holding ~69% of exchange stocks. Kalshi lists short-dated copper contracts (~$6.6/lb) but no 12-month market I could use. FCX fundamentals (company filings): Q2 adj EPS $0.74 beat, 2026 copper 3.1B lbs, unit cost $1.90, net debt $2.1B ex-downstream, Grasberg ramp to ~80% mid-2027 and full by end-2027. At $70.58 the stock is ~17x my 2027E EPS of ~$4.30 and ~7.5x EV/EBITDA, i.e. roughly fair: blended fair value $72. The volume ramp is real upside but mostly known; the main swing factor is copper, which is at a record that major banks expect to fade. I centered the 12-month distribution at a ~$73.5 median (fair value plus small carry from ramp/buybacks), used ~43% vol (slightly below 48% realized as Grasberg de-risks) and fattened the left tail modestly for copper mean-reversion. X/Twitter and Reddit were not reached directly; social-style claims (e.g., data-center skepticism in a digest) were treated as sentiment only. Research was limited to ~12 queries.
